steps.goal: Decide how the cargo and moving DNA bridge relate to the two separated exit routes.
steps.action: Read “Cargo first. Friendship always,” identify the moving bridge and brake/steady pads, and agree which hero will test a bridge control while the partner waits on broad ground.
steps.expected_feedback: Braking or steadying may hold the bridge in a useful position for cargo or traversal. The text names a five-second run and three-second pause, but no input response is shown.

evidence.claim: Visible subtitle and dialogue mention cargo first and a five-second/three-second bridge cycle.
Moving bridge, ANY BRAKE label, PAC STEADY pad, and separated areas are visible.

steps.goal: Test whether the moving bridge can be stopped and used to reach the next platform.
steps.action: Hypothesis: Isp approaches the visible brake control and tests it while Pac observes whether the bridge pauses or changes position.
steps.expected_feedback: A brake cue suggests the bridge may stop or stabilize; no control or outcome is demonstrated.

evidence.claim: ISP-labeled route and ANY BRAKE pad are visible beside the moving bridge.

steps.goal: Use the steady pad or bridge state to support the partner and reach Pac’s exit route.
steps.action: Hypothesis: Pac holds or activates the orange steady pad while Isp crosses, then uses the stabilized bridge or a separate route to proceed.
steps.expected_feedback: The pad may steady tissue and the bridge may become easier to cross; the exact effect and whether holding is required remain unknown.

evidence.claim: PAC STEADY label and Pac exit are visible on the right side of the bridge.

steps.goal: Move any required cargo and reach both matching exits.
steps.action: Coordinate cargo handling only if route feedback or a locked path requires it, then route each hero to the matching exit.
steps.expected_feedback: Both matching exits complete the level; the packet does not demonstrate whether cargo is mandatory or collectible-only.
